label: Origin relation: a real relation of a thing to another as to the principle of its being
term: is really related to as to the principle of its being, at a moment (Lean `OriginRelation.RelatedAt`)
definition: OriginRelation.RelatedAt v x g t: in history v, at moment t, x bears a real relation to g as to the principle of its being (esse). Explicitly identified PRIMITIVE relation; no axiom constrains it. Its bearer is the subject and its term is g. It is a real relation of x, not a relation of reason, and it may be non-mutual: g need bear no real relation back. It names no action of g at t: whether the term is acting at t is the separate open premise TermGives, and whether the term exists at t is the separate open premise TermCoexists. Ordinary meaning: a son is related to his father as to a principle of his being, and so is a moved thing to its mover while it is being moved. Distinguished from the tenseless EsseReceivedIn (DEF-ESSE-RECEIVED-IN; receiver and received act, no term), from BeingGiving.GivesAt (definition 158301bc; the agent side, an occurrent giving), from the tenseless CausesIn (a cause of esse, no moment), and from co-presence (an existing thing need not be the term of any relation).
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred, introduced for the relational-receipt test (docs/notes/sustaining-vs-existential-inertia.md, section 6). It is modelled after ST I q.45 a.3 co. ('creatio in creatura non sit nisi relatio quaedam ad Creatorem, ut ad principium sui esse'), ad 1 (the creature's relation to God is real, God's to the creature of reason only) and ad 3 (the creature is the subject of the relation and prior to it in being), read in the pinned Leonine witness passage fb7bd7bb, and after ST I q.13 a.7 co. (passage 12d8ecc5): relations consequent on action and passion, 'ut motivum et mobile, pater et filius', are real; relations between a being and a non-being are of reason only. No claim attributes this definition to those passages, because the Lean relation is time-indexed and the texts do not index the creature's relation to moments. Structural properties: none built in (not functional in g, no persistence, no tie to presence or giving). OPEN: whether the creature's relation to God is of the present-action type (mover and moved) or the completed-action type (father and son); that is the content of TermGives. Would be sourced by a passage that states the creature's relation to the principle of its being as obtaining at each moment of its existence.
